evals.prompt: On the budgets page, stepping back through months shows 'Loading budgets…' on every click, and most people go back one month at a time to compare. Make that feel instant, including the first time a month is opened.
evals.expected_output: Defines the budgets query once with `queryOptions()` next to `useBudgets` in use-finance-data.ts, spreads it into `useBudgets` with `placeholderData: keepPreviousData`, and prefetches the previous month with `queryClient.prefetchQuery(budgetsQuery(previousMonth))` on focus and pointer enter of the Previous month control (without making MonthPicker, which the overview and transactions screens also use, fetch budgets there), adds a test, and updates agents/conventions.md › Client patterns because `queryOptions` becomes a house pattern. Skill-only: #2 (references/data-fetching.md › Reads 7), #3 focus as well as hover (data-fetching.md PreviousMonthButton example, references/bundle.md › bundle-preload), #6 (SKILL.md › Keep the docs true names queryOptions).
assertions: useBudgets keeps QueryKeys.budgets(month) as its key and sets placeholderData: keepPreviousData (imported from @tanstack/react-query), so the previous month stays on screen while the next one loads

The budgets query is defined once with TanStack Query's queryOptions() in use-finance-data.ts and that definition is spread into both useBudgets and the prefetch call, so the key and queryFn are not written a second time

The previous month's budgets are put in the cache before the click with queryClient.prefetchQuery (or ensureQueryData), and the trigger also fires for keyboard users (on focus of the Previous month control, or whenever the month changes), not only on mouse hover
No fetch call, useEffect-based loading or copy of query data into useState is introduced, and the month change does not await the prefetch
A test covers the new behaviour, for example that focusing or hovering Previous month fills QueryKeys.budgets(previous month), or that the old month stays rendered while the new one is pending
agents/conventions.md › Client patterns is updated in the same change to describe the shared queryOptions definition (and prefetching on intent) as the house pattern

evals.prompt: In the review inbox, clicking Done or picking a category waits for the server before the row disappears, and the budgets page lags behind too. Make it instant: remove the row straight away and, in the same step, add the transaction's amount to that category's spent figure in the cached budgets so the progress bars are right immediately. If the save fails, nothing should look changed.
evals.expected_output: Makes the row removal optimistic in ReviewInbox: onMutate cancels and snapshots the review list query (QueryKeys.transactions({ limit: '500', needsReview: '1' }) or the ['transactions'] prefix), writes a filtered copy, onError restores the snapshot and toasts error.message, and useRefreshFinance() refreshes every FinanceKeys query afterwards. It declines to edit the cached budgets: spent and progress are SQL over the ledger and per currency (the transaction's currency and month may not match a budget row, transfers never count, the old category's spent would also change), so they come back from the refetch. The test checks the row is gone before the mocked categorizeTransaction resolves and returns when it rejects. Skill-only: #4 (references/data-fetching.md › Optimistic updates: only fields the row owns, never balances, totals or budget progress on the client).
assertions: onMutate cancels in-flight queries for the review list (QueryKeys.transactions({ limit: '500', needsReview: '1' }) or the ['transactions'] prefix) before snapshotting it and writing a copy without the row (filter or equivalent, the cached array is not mutated)
onError writes the snapshot back so the row reappears and shows the error message in a toast
After the write, useRefreshFinance() (or invalidation of every FinanceKeys query) runs so budgets and the summary are refetched from the API

No budget, spent, progress or summary value is written into the cache on the client (no setQueryData or setQueriesData on the budgets or summary keys), and the answer explains that these figures come from the ledger and are per currency, so they are refreshed from the server instead of computed optimistically
The review-inbox test covers both paths: the row is gone before the mocked categorizeTransaction resolves, and it is back after the mocked call rejects

Keeps the project barrels (agents/components.md, ESLint) and does not add lucide-react, recharts or date-fns to optimizePackageImports because Next already optimizes them. Keeps the chart and screen tests working by mocking next/dynamic or waiting with findBy, and does not claim a size win it did not measure. Skill-only: #3 reserved space, #4 tests (references/bundle.md › bundle-dynamic-imports), #5 Next's default optimizePackageImports list (bundle.md › bundle-barrel-imports), #6 (SKILL.md › Verify).
assertions: The recharts code is no longer statically reachable from the overview screen: next/dynamic is declared at module scope (in overview.tsx or inside the chart components, either is acceptable), never inside a component body

Each dynamic import uses a literal path to a component folder or to a private file in the same component folder and selects the named export (for example with .then); no file inside another component's folder is imported

While the chunk loads, a fallback (for example a Spinner) occupies the chart's reserved space, such as the chart-frame height, so the layout does not shift; ssr: false appears only in 'use client' files
The existing chart or overview tests keep working, and the answer says how: they mock next/dynamic or wait for the lazily loaded chart with findBy or waitFor

Project barrels and folder imports are kept with agents/components.md or its ESLint rules given as the reason, and lucide-react, recharts or date-fns are not added to optimizePackageImports nor deep-imported, because Next.js already optimizes them
The answer does not claim a bundle-size or load-time improvement it did not measure: it either reports measured build output or says it was not measured and how to measure it
